- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or misses upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% to capture rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay downward adjustment by 1–2 days or reduce magnitude.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early 30-day horizon; if recent 7-day average is above 30-day average, forecast should be slightly above that average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment trend 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment turns neutral or bullish.
- If sentiment is flat or low (0.3–0.6), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for hidden volatility or policy surprises.
